title: Test coverage: measuring it and knowing what it does not tell you

videos.script: After five lessons of tests, a fair question is what they leave out. Coverage answers it: which statements ran while the tests did. {{measure}} One flag gives a number. Another gives the map, function by function, and three functions have lines nobody reached. Two of them are one real gap: a document that fails half way through. You close it with a reader from the standard library that fails on purpose. The third gap stays open, and the lesson says why. {{misses}} Then what a covered line does not tell you. A function at full coverage panics on the first negative number anybody passes. You fix it, and the number never moves. {{program}} Last, coverage of a whole program. The package gets a small command, built to record its own coverage, and two real runs show which parts of it a user actually reaches. {{close}} That ends the course: concurrency, the standard library, and the tests that hold both to what they promise.
